q: Which city was the very first capital of Canada?
funFact: Kingston was the capital for three years, starting in 1841.

q: Kingston's nickname comes from its grey stone buildings. What is it?
funFact: Workers dug the pale limestone right out of the ground nearby.

q: Fort Henry was built to guard which famous canal?
funFact: The Rideau Canal is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

q: The Rideau Canal connects Kingston to which city?
funFact: In winter part of that canal in Ottawa becomes a skating rink.

q: What is the name of the Fort Henry Guard's goat mascot?
funFact: Every mascot goat gets the same name: David.

q: Kingston sits where Lake Ontario pours into which river?
funFact: From here the water flows all the way to the Atlantic Ocean.

q: Which Great Lake is Kingston built beside?
funFact: Lake Ontario is the smallest Great Lake, but very deep.

q: What is the group of islands just east of Kingston called?
funFact: There are actually more than 1,800 islands in that stretch.

q: What very loud thing do soldiers fire at Fort Henry?
funFact: Cover your ears — you feel a cannon in your chest.

q: Canada's first prime minister grew up in Kingston. Who was he?
funFact: His old Kingston house is still standing today.
